source: KICD Agriculture, First Published 2017; Revised 2024 (text layer)
status: outcomes from KICD's text, word for word; skills, prerequisites and misconceptions not yet mapped

learning_experiences: discuss and identify sites in the school or community that have poor soil for crop growth,
construct a pit, a site or a structure for damping plant residue and suitable food remains and organic kitchen wastes in school,
plant crop in a residue pit to observe and appreciate soil improvement from accumulated organic wastes.
key_inquiry_questions: How can we improve the soil using suitable organic wastes?
sub_strands.core_competences: Critical thinking and problem solving: observation skills as learners identify appropriate sites for soil improvement.
sub_strands.values: Unity: collaborative skills as learners construct organic waste pit for soil improvement.
sub_strands.pcis: Environmental conservation as learners recycle organic wastes through the organic waste pit.
sub_strands.links: Learners relate the construction and use of organic waste pit to waste management skills learnt in Science and Technology.

outcomes.text: identify sites for soil improvement in the school or community
construct organic waste pit for soil improvement
demonstrate use of plant remains for soil improvement

learning_experiences: use devices or other resources to search for information on ways of water conservation such as mulching, cover cropping and shading in kitchen and backyard gardening,
practise various ways of conserving water in farming (mulching, shading, cover cropping) within the school,
experiment mulching (mulch some crops and leave others un-mulched and compare moisture conservation),
make presentations to share experiences on importance of conserving water (mulching, cover cropping and shading) in kitchen and backyard gardening activities.
key_inquiry_questions: How can we conserve soil water in household gardening practices?
sub_strands.core_competences: Leaning to learn: learning independently as learners engage in self-driven tasks for water conservation.
sub_strands.values: Integrity: taking personal responsibility in the use of digital devices while searching for information on water conservation.
sub_strands.pcis: Environmental awareness as the learners conserve soil moisture through gardening practices.
sub_strands.links: Learners relate water conservation to knowledge on natural resources in the environment learnt in Social Studies.

outcomes.text: identify ways of conserving water for household gardening
practice water conservation within the school or community
appreciate importance of conserving water in the community

learning_experiences: watch video clips or listen to a resource person on safe ways of repelling wild animals (such as use of smoke, smells) to avoid damage on property (crops and domestic animals) and live better with wild animals,
innovate safe ways of repelling small wild animals (smoke, use of smell repellant or any other),
discuss and make presentations on importance of conserving wild animals in the environment.
key_inquiry_questions: How can we repel wild animals to avoid destruction of property?
sub_strands.core_competences: Critical thinking and problem solving: evaluation and decision making skill as learners explore ways of solving destruction of property by wild animals.
sub_strands.values: Patriotism: learners show love for the environment by conserving animal diversity.
sub_strands.pcis: Conservation of biodiversity as learners appreciate cultural heritage in their community.
sub_strands.links: Learners relate conservation of wild animals to conservation of natural resources learnt in Social Studies.

outcomes.text: identify ways of repelling wild animals to avoid damage of property
repel wild animals to avoid destruction of property
appreciate importance of living better with wild animals

learning_experiences: brainstorm and share experiences on gardening practices of vegetables in a nursery bed,
prepare a nursery bed (container or ground nursery), sow vegetable seeds and take care of the seedlings,
transplant vegetable seedlings and take care of the seedlings,
make class presentations on importance of growing vegetables as a source of food for animals and humans.
key_inquiry_questions: How does growing vegetables contribute to food production?
sub_strands.core_competences: Self-efficacy: self-drive as learners undertake projects to grow vegetable crops.
sub_strands.values: Social justice: learners foster fairness in sharing and undertaking of duties in the vegetable production project.
sub_strands.pcis: Financial literacy as the learners appreciate saving on cost at school or family level by growing own vegetables.
sub_strands.links: Learners relate growing of vegetables to social economic activities in the community learnt through Social Studies.

outcomes.text: identify gardening practices in growing vegetables
establish a nursery bed for vegetables
care for vegetable seedlings after transplanting
appreciate the importance of vegetables in provision of healthy meals

learning_experiences: brainstorm and share experiences on the uses of domestic animals in food production (bees, rabbits, camels, fish, pigs, donkeys, dogs and cats),
match domestic animals to their uses,
make class presentations on importance of domestic animals in various food production processes while relating contributions of all the scoped animals.
key_inquiry_questions: How are domestic animals important in food production?
sub_strands.core_competences: Communication: speaking clearly and effectively as learners make presentations on uses of domestic animals in food production.
sub_strands.values: Patriotism: appreciating own culture by recognising diversity of domestic animals reared in the country.
sub_strands.pcis: Food and nutrition security as the learners appreciate the direct and indirect uses of domestic animals in food production.
sub_strands.links: Learners relate the rearing and uses of domestic animals as socio-economic activity learnt in Social Studies.

outcomes.text: identify uses of various domestic animals in food production processes
relate various domestic animals to their uses
appreciate the importance of domestic animals in food production

learning_experiences: brainstorm and share experiences on methods of preserving and storing cereals and pulses (such as sun drying, use of ashes, use of airtight containers) at household level,
preserve and store cereals and pulses using methods such as sun drying, use of ash and airtight containers.
make class presentations to share experiences on importance of preserving and storing cereals and pulses.
key_inquiry_questions: How does preservation and storage of cereals and pulses enhance food security?
sub_strands.core_competences: Critical thinking and problem solving: exploring ways of preserving and storing cereals and pulses to prevent spoilage.
sub_strands.values: Unity: taking turns while undertaking tasks in preservation of cereals and pulses.
sub_strands.pcis: Food and nutrition security as learners preserve available cereals and pulses to prevent food spoilage.
sub_strands.links: Learners relate skills in preservation of cereals and pulses to farming activities in the community learnt in Social Studies.

outcomes.text: describe methods of preserving cereals and pulses in the locality
preserve cereals and pulses for food security
appreciate the importance of preserving cereals and pulses for food security

learning_experiences: search and share information on functions of food nutrients (carbohydrates, vitamins, proteins, fats),
use samples of food materials and photographs to categorise foods based on their major nutrients (protein rich foods, carbohydrates rich foods, vitamins and minerals rich foods),
use print and digital devices to search for information on various nutritional diseases and disorders such as kwashiorkor, marasmus, goiter and anaemia,
make class presentations on the importance of various nutrients in the body.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is the knowledge of food nutrients important in food production?
sub_strands.core_competences: Digital literacy: interaction with digital technologies while searching for information on food nutrients.
sub_strands.values: Unity: respect of each other’s opinions while making presentations on importance of nutrients in the body.
sub_strands.pcis: Health promotion as learners learn the importance of food nutrients in the body.
sub_strands.links: Learners relate food nutrients to prevention of non-communicable diseases learnt in Science and Technology.

outcomes.text: explain functions of food nutrients in the body
categorise foods based on their major nutrients
identify nutritional diseases and disorders associated with poor eating habits
appreciate the importance of various nutrients in the body

learning_experiences: watch video clip or demonstration on dry fat frying and deep frying methods of cooking,
cook foods using dry fat frying and deep frying methods,
serve foods that have been cooked through dry fat frying and deep frying methods.
key_inquiry_questions: How can we cook foods using dry fat frying and deep frying methods?
sub_strands.core_competences: Learning to learn: self-discipline as learners work cautiously to fry foods.
sub_strands.values: Responsibility: taking personal initiative to observe safety as learners handle hot oils and equipment in frying foods.
sub_strands.pcis: Safety and security for self and others as learners handle hot equipment and fat while frying food.
sub_strands.links: Learners relate safety and first aid from burns and scald to knowledge learnt in Science and Technology.

outcomes.text: describe various methods of cooking food
cook foods using various methods
embrace dry fat frying and deep frying in food production

learning_experiences: discuss and share experiences on aspects of good grooming (dressing and etiquette) for different occasions,
demonstrate different ways of dressing and etiquette for different activities,
conduct class modelling on different ways of dressing and etiquette to appreciate good grooming habits for different activities.
key_inquiry_questions: How does good grooming promote personal hygiene?
sub_strands.core_competences: Self-efficacy: identification of self as learners develop good grooming habits.
sub_strands.values: Respect: positive regard for self and others as learners adopt good grooming habits.
sub_strands.pcis: Health promotion as learners adopt preventive health practices through good grooming habits.
sub_strands.links: Learners relate good grooming habits to self-discovery learnt in Social Studies.

outcomes.text: describe good grooming as a daily health habit
practice good grooming as a daily health habit
appreciate good grooming as a healthy habit

learning_experiences: discuss and share experiences on surfaces made from different materials such as glass, wooden, earthen floors, cemented and tiled,
clean different types of surfaces such as glass, wooden, earthen floors, cemented and tiled,
maintain cleanliness of surfaces in the school to appreciate living in clean environment.
key_inquiry_questions: How do you clean surfaces made from different materials?
sub_strands.core_competences: Communication and collaboration: listening and speaking skills using facts to support opinions in brainstorming on home hygiene.
sub_strands.values: Unity: taking turns in activities while learners participate in cleaning surfaces.
sub_strands.pcis: Safety of self and others while learners clean various types of surfaces at home or school.
sub_strands.links: Learners relate cleaning of surfaces to prevention of contamination and prevention of spreading communicable diseases learnt in Science and Technology.

outcomes.text: identify surfaces made from different materials in home environment
clean different types of surfaces in the home environment
appreciate living in a clean home environment to promote healthy living

learning_experiences: watch a clip or observe a demonstration on how to launder a cotton item (white and fast coloured cotton),
launder a white and fast coloured cotton item,
practice laundering of white and fast coloured items at home to appreciate the importance of laundry work for personal hygiene.
key_inquiry_questions: How does laundering cotton items promote hygiene?
sub_strands.core_competences: Leaning to learn: sharing of ideas when carrying out activities with peers in laundering cotton items.
sub_strands.values: Responsibility: taking care of personal items in the laundering of cotton items.
sub_strands.pcis: Personal hygiene as they clean cotton items to promote health.
sub_strands.links: Learners relate personal hygiene to communicable diseases learnt in Science and Technology.

outcomes.text: describe how to launder a cotton item
launder a cotton item for personal hygiene
appreciate importance of laundry work for hygiene purposes

learning_experiences: use pictures, samples of garments, video clips and charts to identify stitches such as back stitch and running stitch used in repairing garment,
make samples of running and back stitches,
use back stitch and running stitch to repair gaping seam,
make use of back stitch and running stitch repair their daily wear.
sub_strands.core_competences: Critical thinking and problem solving: evaluation and decision making skills as learners explore ways of repairing garment.
sub_strands.values: Responsibility: taking care of personal items through repairing of gaping seams.
sub_strands.pcis: Financial literacy as learners save costs by repairing own clothes.
sub_strands.links: Learners relate cloth repairing skills such as choice and use of colours to aesthetic skills learnt in Creative Arts.

outcomes.text: identify stitches used in repairing garment
make samples of stitches used to repair garments
use the stitches to repair gaping seam
adopt the use of stitches to repair of garments

learning_experiences: watch or observe stimulus materials (video clips, pictures and photographs) on innovative gardening practices to differentiate between vertical and horizontal gardens,
use sacks, plastic bottles, walls, plastic pipes among others to construct vertical and horizontal gardens for growing crops,
use the vertical and horizontal gardens to grow appropriate crop.
key_inquiry_questions: How can gardening be done on vertical and horizontal spaces?
sub_strands.core_competences: Creativity and imagination: designing and assembling skills as learners innovate vertical and horizontal gardens.
sub_strands.values: Unity: team spirit as learners take turns in constructing vertical and horizontal gardens.
sub_strands.pcis: Environmental awareness as learners utilise limited spaces through use of vertical and horizontal gardens.
sub_strands.links: Learners relate designing structures and use of craft tools and equipment to skills learnt in Creative Arts.

outcomes.text: distinguish between horizontal and vertical innovative gardening
construct innovative gardens for growing crops
adopt the use of innovative gardens in growing crops

indicators.indicator: Ability to describe conservation of resources in the environment: (soil, water and wild animals).

levels.EE: The learner describes conservation measures of three resources in the environment.
levels.ME: The learner describes conservation measures of two resources in the environment.
levels.AE: The learner describes conservation measures of one resource in the environment.
levels.BE: The learner makes a partial description of a resource in the environment.

indicators.indicator: Ability to conserve resources in the environment: (soil, water and wild animals).

levels.EE: The learner conserves three resources in the environment.
levels.ME: The learner conserves two resources in the environment.
levels.AE: The learner conserves one resource in the environment.
levels.BE: The learner partially conserves a resource in the environment.

indicators.indicator: Ability to show critical thinking and problem solving in conservation of resources: (seeks information, finds help when needed, explores possible solutions, completes task).

levels.EE: The learner shows four indicators of critical thinking and problem solving in conservation of resources.
levels.ME: The learner shows three indicators of critical thinking and problem solving in conservation of resources.
levels.AE: The learner shows two indicators of critical thinking and problem solving in conservation of resources.
levels.BE: The learner shows less than two indicators of critical thinking and problem solving in conservation of resources.

indicators.indicator: Ability to describe food production processes: (growing vegetables, use of domestic animals, preservation of cereals and pulses, cooking by frying). Ability to apply food production processes at household level. (growing vegetables, use of domestic animals, preservation of cereals and pulses, cooking by frying).

levels.EE: The learner describes four food production processes. Applies four food production processes at household level.
levels.ME: The learner describes three food production processes. Applies three food production processes at household level.
levels.AE: The learner describes two food production processes. Applies two food production processes at household level.
levels.BE: The learner describes less than two food production processes. Applies less than two food production processes at household level.

indicators.indicator: Ability to upholds integrity in carrying out activities of food production processes: (commitment to tasks, is honest, has prudence in use of resources and accountable).

levels.EE: The learner upholds four indicators of integrity in carrying out activities of production processes.
levels.ME: The learner upholds three indicators of integrity in carrying out activities of production processes.
levels.AE: The learner upholds two indicators of integrity in carrying out activities of production processes.
levels.BE: The learner upholds less than two indicators of integrity in carrying out activities of production processes.

indicators.indicator: Ability to describe hygiene practices as a daily health habit: (good grooming, home hygiene, laundering items).

levels.EE: The learner describes three hygiene practices observed as daily health habit.
levels.ME: The learner describes two hygiene practices observed as daily health habit.
levels.AE: The learner describes one hygiene practice observed as daily health habit.
levels.BE: The learner gives partial description of hygiene practices observed as daily health habit.

indicators.indicator: Ability to carry out hygiene practices as a daily health habit. (good grooming, home hygiene, laundering items).

levels.EE: The learner carries out three hygiene practices observed as daily health habit. (good grooming, home hygiene, laundering items) as daily health with specific attention to details.
levels.ME: The learner carries out two hygiene practices observed as daily health habit.
levels.AE: The learner carries out one hygiene practice observed as daily health habit.
levels.BE: The learner partially carries out a hygiene practice observed as daily health habit.

indicators.indicator: Ability to exhibit responsibility in hygiene practices: (care for self, own property and others, observes safety and is self-directed).

levels.EE: The learner exhibits four aspects of responsibility in hygiene practices.
levels.ME: The learner exhibits three aspects of responsibility in hygiene practices.
levels.AE: The learner exhibits two aspects of responsibility in hygiene practices.
levels.BE: The learner exhibits less than two aspects of responsibility in hygiene practices.

indicators.indicator: Ability to explain various techniques in production processes: (repair of garments, construction of vertical, and construction of horizontal gardens).

levels.EE: The learner explains three production techniques.
levels.ME: The learner explains two production techniques.
levels.AE: The learner explains one production technique.
levels.BE: The learner gives partial explanation of a production technique.

indicators.indicator: Ability to apply various techniques in production processes: (repair of garments, construction of vertical, and construction of horizontal gardens).

levels.EE: The learner applies three techniques in various production processes.
levels.ME: The learner applies two techniques in various production processes.
levels.AE: The learner applies one technique in various production processes.
levels.BE: The learner partially applies a technique in a production process.

indicators.indicator: Ability to exhibit creativity and imagination in carrying out various production techniques: (Generates new ideas, combines different concepts, uses creativity in work contexts, actualises imagined ideas).

levels.EE: The learner exhibits four indicators of creativity and imagination in various production techniques.
levels.ME: The learner exhibits three indicators of creativity and imagination in various production techniques.
levels.AE: The learner exhibits two indicators of creativity and imagination in various production techniques.
levels.BE: The learner exhibits less than two indicators of creativity and imagination in various production techniques.
